prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1025; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim number.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving on the main road in Pearland, heading toward the shopping center. It was raining a little.
Q: What happened right before impact?
A: A car came over into my lane. I braked and turned the wheel, but we still hit head-on. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jolt me.
Q: How fast were you traveling?
A: Maybe twenty-five miles an hour, maybe less. Traffic was slow.
Q: Did your airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. The seatbelt locked and I hit my head on the side window.
Q: Did you seek medical attention after the accident?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care that evening. They said I have a concussion and told me to rest.
Q: What symptoms are you still experiencing?
A: Headaches mostly, and I get dizzy if I look at screens too long. I'm also more tired than usual and I've had trouble concentrating at work.
Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: I've taken a few days off and I'm working shortened hours now. My doctor has me on light duty.
Q: Do you have any prior head injuries or conditions that affect your memory or concentration?
A: No, nothing I can recall.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm hoping to get my car repaired soon. I still need it for getting to my medical appointments.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Thanks.
